Hi Sofia,

We filled out the self-serve interest form and selected "Dedicated capacity" as our preferred deployment. A few quick details so you have context before the call:
- Primary workload: clinical document summarization and triage (batch + real-time endpoints)
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~120 requests/sec; peak bursts up to ~350 RPS for short windows
- Avg prompt size: 400–700 tokens; expect some long-context replies up to ~2,000 tokens
- P95 latency target: <= 250ms for single-turn generation (we're flexible but this is what product requires)

Would love a brief technical demo + capacity planning conversation to understand fit and any pre-reqs. We're based on PDT and can do windows Tue/Thu 10–12 or Wed 14–16 next week.

Thanks for confirming, Tom and team — looking forward to the call. A couple of technical pre-call asks so I can size the Dedicated pool and prepare a demo environment that mirrors your production profile:

1) Could you share 5–10 representative sample prompts and a rough distribution of response lengths (short <256 tokens, medium 256–1024, long >1024)? A redacted sample is fine.
2) Do you expect streaming responses or batch (synchronous) only? Streaming has different kernel and socket expectations.
3) Any constraints on model family? (open Llama variants, Mistral, etc.) If you're undecided, we can demo with a low-latency open model and show quantization options.
4) For IP allowlisting + mTLS, please confirm whether you'll terminate TLS at your edge (we'll need certificate thumbprints) or if we should expect client cert rotation via an API.

I attached a filled example of the pre-call checklist (sample values) and a short ops runbook stub. If you drop sample-prompts.txt and confirm streaming vs sync, I'll run an internal perf projection and bring a proposed GPU pool (instance class + expected tokens/sec) to the walkthrough.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

[Attachment: redwood-dedicated-precall-checklist.pdf (annotated)]

Hi all — attaching the sample prompts and a completed checklist (redacted). Answers inline:
- Prompt distribution: ~60% short (<256), 30% medium (256–1024), 10% long (>1024)
- Streaming: primary paths are synchronous API calls; a small subset will use streaming for multi-part explanations (we can simulate)
- Model family: we'd prefer to evaluate a tested open model rather than a proprietary hosted-only stack; lower-precision quantized suggestions are welcome if latency improves
- TLS: we terminate at our edge and will provide cert thumbprints; we also need a SOC2 evidence checklist for procurement (Tom is copying procurement on follow-ups).

Thanks for the quick turnaround — see you on 9/21 at 10:30 PDT. I'll leave the calendar invite acceptance from our side once Sofia sends it.

Best,
Susan Park
